slots.label: storage-size misconception
slots.description: Working memory is just a smaller hard drive where temporary memories sit until moved unchanged into long-term memory.
slots.repair: Working memory is active use and attention, not merely a passive staging folder.
slots.repairQuestion: What makes working memory 'working' when you solve a mental arithmetic problem?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says information is actively held, manipulated, or attended to for a task.

slots.label: automatic-transfer misconception
slots.description: Everything held briefly in working memory automatically becomes long-term memory.
slots.repair: Many working-memory contents fade when no longer needed; durable learning requires encoding, practice, or meaningful connection.
slots.repairQuestion: Why might you forget a verification code seconds after using it?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says temporary information can be discarded or not encoded into long-term memory.

slots.label: long-term-always-conscious misconception
slots.description: If something is in long-term memory, it is constantly present in conscious thought.
slots.repair: Long-term memory can be stored without being active; retrieval brings it into working memory when needed.
slots.repairQuestion: Where is your childhood address before someone asks for it?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says it is stored in long-term memory but not active until retrieved.

slots.text: What makes working memory 'working' when you solve a mental arithmetic problem?
Why might you forget a verification code seconds after using it?
Where is your childhood address before someone asks for it?

Working memory is a small, active workspace for current thinking; long-term memory is durable storage of knowledge and experiences. Remembered knowledge must be retrieved into working memory to be used. Working-memory limits matter for learning, and long-term knowledge can reduce load by organizing information into meaningful chunks.
